inputs.theme: Colors and Shapes: finding color and shape all around us

idea.title: Chalk Color Walk Outside
idea.summary: Toddlers walk and crouch along a short outdoor path, matching big color and shape shapes drawn in chalk or taped to the ground. The educator stays close and names what the children find.
setup: Check the outdoor area is clear of sticks, rocks, and anything small enough to go in a mouth.
Using chalk, draw large simple shapes (circle, square, triangle) in red, blue, and yellow along a short path. Keep them big and well apart.
Cut a few large colored paper shapes to match, and tape a few of them to the fence or a low post at toddler eye level.
Put the soft mat near the start for children who want to sit and rest.

tiers.label: Walk, point, and name
steps: Invite children to walk slowly along the path with you, holding hands if they wish.
At each chalk shape, stop, point, and say the color and the shape out loud, like 'Red circle! Round like a ball.'
Let children point, stomp, or crouch to touch a shape, copying your words as they can.
Give a scarf to any child who wants to wave it over a shape they find.
Finish at the mat with a stretch, reaching up high and down low, while you sing a short color song.
tiers.stretch: Ask a child to walk to a red shape you name, or to hop over the blue one.

safety: Keep the adult within arm's reach of every toddler at all times, especially near the fence and any steps.
Use only chalk and tape meant for children; check for wet paint or loose tape ends before the walk.
Check the ground for broken glass, sharp edges, and loose items before each use.
An educator supervises the whole time.
Check the space and every material before you start.
watch_for: Notice which toddlers move with confidence and which prefer to stay close to you, and record their balance and steadiness.
Note whether a child repeats a color or shape word after you, and which words they say on their own.
talk: What color is this one? Can you show me?
Is this shape round like a ball, or does it have corners?
Where else do you see a circle outside today?
idea.home_idea: Draw a few big circles and squares on the sidewalk or on paper with chalk, then walk or hop between them while naming each color together.
